title: extcap: Restore logging for plugins in stand-alone mode

notes.body: mentioned in merge request !5322

It do not core dump, but doesn't work as expected. When --debug and --debug-file is used, only debug messages are written to the file. Other levels are on console. Therefore you (developer) do not see full context.

I think that my patch !5291 works as expected. There is only issue when just --debug is used from GUI. But I think that anyone who will issue --debug will know why they is doing it and will read documentation. So they learn that they must use --debug-file.

> I think that my patch !5291 works as expected. There is only issue when just --debug is used from GUI. But I think that anyone who will issue --debug will know why they is doing it and will read documentation. So they learn that they must use --debug-file.

I must disagree. It won't be long until someone rightfully opens a bug against that footgun. But it is a difference of opinion, it would be nice to hear from others as well.

I see, but it has no solution when you have two parameters which depends on each other.

So what about remove --debug and --debug-file and create --debug-output. Default would be empty, mean no debug.
If you will use --debug-output=-, it will be routed to console. If you will use --debug-output=path, output will be sent to file. For '-' colouring will be enabled.

I expect that --debug-output=- will not be used from GUI.

Something like that sounds good. I'm not sure about the details but shouldn't be too difficult to find a solution that can accommodate both use cases.

I also wanted to add console logging from the GUI (independent of file logging), but that is even more complicated (for later).
But we should take into account that environment variables are there and they work independently on command line parameters...

> It do not core dump, but doesn't work as expected. When --debug and --debug-file is used, only debug messages are written to the file. Other levels are on console. Therefore you (developer) do not see full context.

If I'm not mistaken this is how these options used to work. So if it improves things (i.e: it allows using the console stand-alone), even if it is not perfect, I would like to merge it. Without excluding further work by you.

> It do not core dump, but doesn't work as expected. When --debug and --debug-file is used, only debug messages are written to the file. Other levels are on console. Therefore you (developer) do not see full context.

This is also the correct behavior. In this case errors and warnings must be written to stderr and reported to the GUI. Debug goes to file. I think it is working as the original extcap authors expected.

commits_data.title: Extcap: Improve the log handler logic
commits_data.message:
Extcap: Improve the log handler logic

If we have a log file write everything to the file, to provide
a complete picture in the log.

Debug information cannot be written to the parent process when
running in child mode.

commits_data.title: extcap: Register log handler conditionally
commits_data.message:
extcap: Register log handler conditionally

This matches the original implementation and allows displaying
logs to the console, including debug information, when running
an extcap from the CLI for testing and development purposes.

This should make extcap logging bug-for-bug compatible with the
behavior before dc7f0b88bb.

commits_data.title: wslog: Use stdout for debug messages
commits_data.message:
wslog: Use stdout for debug messages

Imitate the GLib logic for selecting the console output stream
according to the log level. Levels MESSAGE and above go to
stderr. INFO and below go to stdout, unless stderr is chosen
using ws_log_console_writer_set_use_stderr().

It turns out some old extcap code was subtly dependending
on this behavior.
